x: B is the odd one out: the Dual Government arose from a LACK of British manpower for civil administration, not to provide adequate manpower. Avoiding Parliament's scrutiny, keeping other Europeans paying duties to the 'Nawab' and hiding imperial ambitions were the actual reasons.

Cornwallis's coalition won at Seringapatam in 1792 and Tipu sued for peace. A and B swap the battles: Pollilur (1780) was Haidar and Tipu's defeat of Baillie, Porto Novo (1781) was Eyre Coote's win over Haidar; D is wrong because the British won in 1799 and Tipu was killed.

Per these notes (CDX), Jogipantulu used the Gollapudi mutiny to get the Circars leased to the Company for 15 lakh rupees a year (1766). 9 lakh is the reduced peshkash of the 1768 Treaty of Masulipatnam, and 7 lakh the Guntur payment of 1788.

All three are correct: Provincial Chiefs and Councils at Masulipatnam and Vizagapatnam governed the Circars; the supervising revenue body over these stations is called the 'Board of Revenue' in some notes; and district Collectors replaced the arrangement in 1794, when that body was abolished.

The Madras District Police Act dates to 1859. 1816 is when Munro moved police supervision from judges to Collectors, and 1820 is when the appeal courts' powers were expanded and Munro became Governor.
